lede: Mark swept Week 3 and leads by two. Chicago finished it for him on Monday night with a 38-year-old backup nobody had penciled in.

beats.text: Second sweep of the season and his biggest lead yet. Monday was the strangest part: Caleb Williams out with a hamstring, Tyson Bagent not cleared from concussion protocol until Sunday, so Case Keenum started and threw for 247 with three total touchdowns while the defense took the ball away three times. 27-7 over an unbeaten Philadelphia.

He was a point from second place on Sunday morning. Since then Arizona lost by 24 in Seattle, the Jets went to overtime and lost, and his unbeaten Eagles got dismantled by a backup — with Jalen Hurts leaving for a concussion evaluation. Six points, and a quarterback question going into Week 4.

He owns both sidelines at Detroit–Carolina on Sunday night, his second civil war of the season, so that point is already in. Brian gets the same deal on Monday with Atlanta at New Orleans. Between them, two of the week's sixteen games are decided before kickoff.

Kansas City at Las Vegas. Jon's Chiefs are 3-0 and Mark's Raiders are 3-0, both quietly, and they play each other — so one of them takes a point off the other. Mark leads by two; this is the single game most likely to change that.
